## Final data-grounded hypothesis (primary = full hundred-year-slice PCA)

On the first principal component (PC1) of a **correlation-matrix PCA on the 12 forms of capital across the 39 hundred-year time slices of capital.csv (BCE 4300–500; PC1 = 30.3% of variance, PC2 = 19.5%)**, the **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE, MN group)** and the **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE, SG group)** are **both characterized by strongly negative PC1 scores**.

**Sign convention (explicit):** PC1's sign is arbitrary; I oriented it so the **dominant loading block is positive (net loading sum = +1.38)**. Under this convention “high PC1” means the pole of prestige-metal/accumulation-linked capital — copper/gold (+0.41), pottery decoration (+0.38), hoards/depots (+0.34), hatchet/sword (+0.30), dagger (+0.27), monument size (+0.24), house size (+0.23), monument count (+0.20) — versus the negative pole defined by plain pottery form (−0.35), axes/celts (−0.24), amber (−0.24) and sickle (−0.15). In the capital-grouping frame this is positive = symbolic (metals/weapons) + social (hoards/monuments) + cultural (pottery decoration) + economic (house size) capital, negative = amber, axe/celt and plain-pottery economy.

Under that convention:
- **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE):** PC1 mean **−1.37**, range **−1.78…−0.58**, all five slices negative → characterized by the *negative-PC1 pole*: a deep amber/axe/plain-pottery Neolithic economy with little expression of prestige metals, hoards, weaponry or monument capital.
- **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE):** PC1 mean **−1.12**, range **−1.60…−0.41**, all seven slices negative → remains on the *same negative side* of PC1 but is **modestly higher (less negative)** than the Middle Neolithic; the **3000→2900 BCE transition is a modest upward level shift (PC1 −1.783 → −1.504), not a sign flip**.

**Robustness:** the characterization (MN below YN, both negative) **does not flip** when the near-constant ZSichel is dropped (MN −1.44, YN −1.20). It **does flip when the PCA is restricted to the Neolithic-only window (BCE 4100–2200)**: there PC1 re-orients onto pottery/amber (+, loading ~+0.46/+0.43) vs weapons/monuments (−) and the phases sit on opposite sides (MN +1.81, YN −1.27). I therefore adopt the full hundred-year-slice PCA — the analysis implied by “PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices” — as the primary characterization, and flag the window-sensitivity explicitly.

payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (39 hundred-year BCE slices, 4300-500; parsed German comma decimals). Ran correlation-matrix PCA on the 12 capital-form Z-columns (standardized; eigendecomposition of correlation matrix). Oriented PC1 so the net loading sum >= 0 (dominant loading block positive); reported the oriented PC1 loading vector mapped to symbolic/social/economic/cultural grouping and the PC1 time series attached to groups. Characterized MN (3400-3000) vs Younger Neolithic/SG (2900-2300) by PC1 mean/range and the 3000->2900 transition. Robustness: repeated PCA on Neolithic-only window (4100-2200) and dropping ZSichel (near-constant), noting whether the phase characterization flips. Script: analysis/pca_capital.py; outputs: analysis/capital_pca_outputs.csv, analysis/capital_pca_loadings.csv.
